name: ch11_courier_desk_broker
alt: A courier hands a parcel to a building security guard and leaves, while parcels for a resident on holiday pile up at the desk until she returns.
scene: A wide view of the ground-floor lobby of an Indian apartment building, with a security desk on the left, a lift and a notice board in the background, and the glass entrance door on the right. A courier in a brown uniform cap and a sling bag hands a cardboard parcel across the desk to the security guard (middle-aged, blue uniform, moustache, a register open in front of him); the guard signs the courier's handheld device, and the courier is already turning towards the door, one foot pointing outside, his scooter visible through the glass, not waiting for anything. Behind the guard, on a steel rack against the wall, a tall stack of parcels of different sizes has piled up, all tagged with the same flat number, and a small calendar above the rack shows a week of days ticked off, meaning the resident is away. On the far right, entering through the door a week later, the resident (young woman, travel backpack, sunglasses pushed up, a roller suitcase) smiles and points at her pile. A tiny inset bubble near the rack shows a signed parcel being dropped into a bin while a second flatmate in a hoodie asks for it with a question mark, hinting that once collected it is gone. Bright late-morning light through the door, ordinary daily bustle. Labels: "PRODUCER" above the courier, "BROKER" above the guard's desk, and "QUEUE" beside the stack of parcels.

name: ch11_library_post_office_log
alt: A library keeps books on shelves for searching, a post office hands letters out and keeps none, and a second post office photocopies every letter into a permanent register.
scene: A three-panel illustration separated by thin vertical lines, read left to right. LEFT panel: a quiet public library with tall wooden shelves full of books; an elderly librarian in a cardigan and spectacles helps a student search a card catalogue drawer, and every book stays on its shelf; nobody is told when a new book arrives, shown by a phone on the librarian's desk that stays silent. CENTRE panel: a small Indian post office counter with a red post box outside; a postal clerk in khaki hands the last letter from a pigeon-hole rack to a resident who walks away with it, and the rack is now empty; on the wall a row of private letter boxes, one with a small notification slip sticking out, shows that people are told the moment something arrives. RIGHT panel: the same post office counter, but now the clerk feeds each incoming letter through a photocopier before handing it out, and behind him a thick bound register on a stand grows page by page; a second resident reads an old page of the register while the original letter has already gone home with someone else. Soft daylight through high windows in all three panels, calm civic mood. Labels: "DATABASE" at the top of the left panel, "BROKER" at the top of the centre panel, and "LOG" at the top of the right panel.

name: ch11_toll_lanes_partitions
alt: A four-lane toll plaza where a truck arguing in lane 1 blocks the cars behind it while the other lanes flow, and a fifth toll collector stands idle with no lane.
scene: A highway toll plaza seen from slightly above and in front, with four lanes side by side, each with its own booth and a red-and-white boom barrier. In each booth sits one toll collector in a light blue uniform shirt. In lanes 2, 3 and 4 the barriers are up and cars, an auto-rickshaw and a small van roll through smoothly, with motion lines behind them. In lane 1 a big orange goods truck is stopped at the booth; the truck driver leans out of his window waving a large note while the collector shakes his head and counts small coins, and a long queue of cars waits behind the truck with frustrated drivers honking, small horn symbols floating above their roofs, an hourglass over the queue. To the far right of the plaza, beyond lane 4, a fifth toll collector in the same uniform stands beside an empty patch of road with no booth and no lane, holding his receipt machine and shrugging, idle. A highway sign gantry above the plaza spans the four lanes. Midday sun, hazy dusty highway, mild comic frustration. Labels: "PARTITIONS" on the gantry above the four lanes, "HEAD-OF-LINE BLOCKING" over the stuck queue in lane 1, and "IDLE" beside the fifth collector.

key: A dabbawala team: one slow walker falls
name: ch11_dabbawala_slow_walker
alt: Dabbawalas walk their own routes; one slow walker lags with a growing pile of tiffins while the others deliver on time, and a supervisor sends a helper.
scene: A busy Mumbai street near a railway station at late morning, shown as a wide scene with several parallel walking lanes painted faintly on the road. Four dabbawalas in white kurta-pyjamas and white Gandhi caps each push their own long wooden crate or carry a tray of tiffin carriers on their heads, each in his own lane. Three of them stride briskly ahead towards office buildings on the right, where office workers at the doorways already receive their tiffins. The fourth, an older dabbawala in the bottom lane, walks slowly with a limp, and behind him a pile of tiffin carriers keeps growing on a hand cart, much higher than anyone else's, but the other three lanes are not delayed at all. On the left, a supervisor with a clipboard and a whistle watches from a raised step, a small chart in his hand showing the slow walker's pile rising, and he points a young helper towards him, the helper already running with an empty crate. A clock tower in the background shows a little before lunch time. At the far left edge of the bottom lane, a few very old tiffins are being tipped into a bin, hinting that past a limit they are discarded. Bright sun, warm bustle. Labels: "CONSUMER LAG" over the slow walker's pile, and "MONITOR" beside the supervisor.
